CLOSED as UMBRELLA-SCOPE by D1 batch 84 (2026-09-27). This file is not an authored mapping file and carries zero suggestions. The catalog alias for this identity is the literal string "sinusitis, all types", which is an explicit umbrella claim, and the catalog separately carries chronic-sinusitis (respiratory.json) as a distinct identity that already owns the routes this file would otherwise register. If a later reconciliation splits the umbrella into acute and chronic identities, or elects chronic-sinusitis canonical, this file can be reopened; the evidence preserved below is authoring-quality and was verified against PubMed before the closure was made.

Evidence preserved and NOT registered, in the event this file is reopened. (1) The chronic-sinusitis mood route: a systematic review and meta-analysis of depression and anxiety in chronic rhinosinusitis, which located the pooled prevalence of both in that population, and a separate paper reporting that depressed mood MODULATES the impact of chronic rhinosinusitis symptoms on quality of life, which together establish that the mood routes in this disease group belong to the CHRONIC identity rather than to the umbrella. (2) The chronic-sinusitis cognition route: a 2026 review of the association between allergic rhinitis, chronic sinusitis and cognitive impairment. (3) The ACUTE intracranial route, which is the one route an acute member identity would own and which the umbrella label cannot hold: a case series and literature review of PEDIATRIC SINOGENIC INTRACRANIAL ABSCESSES, a report of Pott's puffy tumour as a rare complication of frontal sinusitis, and a report of life-threatening orbital and intracranial sequelae of odontogenic sinusitis. (4) A literature review of clinical emergency-complicated infections of the middle ear and paranasal sinuses. None of these is registered, and the intracranial ones were additionally withheld on a shared-route screen because the registry already carries mastoiditis -> meningitis and mastoiditis -> brain-abscess, so an unexamined sinusitis route to either target would add a sibling of an existing route without a comparative-scope decision.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 84 (2026-09-27): CLOSED as UMBRELLA-SCOPE, following the gastrointestinal-cancers and reproductive-cancers umbrella dispositions of batch 78, which deferred the umbrella identity and left the routes with the member windows. Three considerations make this the same situation rather than a new one. First, the catalog alias is the literal string "sinusitis, all types", so the identity does not merely overlap chronic-sinusitis, it explicitly claims to contain it. Second, the member identity already owns routes: chronic-sinusitis carries a registered edge to sleep-apnea and, from batch 81, samter-s-triad -> chronic-sinusitis is registered, so an edge from the umbrella to either target would register the same clinical route at a second level of indirection and add a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict. Third, the mood and cognitive evidence located for this disease group is CHRONIC-specific throughout, so placing it under an umbrella label would misattribute chronic-disease evidence to a label that does not distinguish duration.

The previous batch authored INSIDE this disease group two batches ago, which is the strongest argument that the group is being worked correctly: batch 81 authored samter-s-triad -> chronic-sinusitis and disclosed on that edge that chronic rhinosinusitis and asthma are CRITERIA THAT DEFINE the syndrome rather than consequences of it, and that the causation status must disclaim the circular reading. That is exactly the discipline an umbrella identity makes impossible to maintain, because the same edge authored under sinusitis would read as a complication of a general sinusitis label when the located evidence is about a defined chronic syndrome.

NOTE ON AN APPARENT TENSION, recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight: the registry already carries bacterial-rhinitis -> sinusitis and deviated-nasal-septum -> sinusitis, so the graph treats this identity as distinct from chronic-sinusitis and already routes into it. That is not evidence against the umbrella claim; it is evidence that two earlier edges were authored under the umbrella label without addressing it, which is precisely the pattern this closure corrects prospectively. Those two existing edges were NOT altered, because changing the meaning of existing mappings is a reviewed decision rather than a side effect of an authoring batch, and the same caution applies to the eczema and atopic-dermatitis-eczema and rotator-cuff-tear and rotator-cuff-injury duplications, which remain unreconciled.

WITHHELD ROUTES recorded for completeness: sleep-apnea as DUPLICATE-SCOPE, the registry already carrying chronic-sinusitis -> sleep-apnea and the sleep-apnea target already holding 21 registered incoming edges; depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder as MEMBER-WINDOW-OWNED and SCOPE-MISMATCHED, the located anchors being chronic-rhinosinusitis-specific; meningitis and brain-abscess as SHARED-ROUTE pending a comparative-scope decision against the existing mastoiditis routes; and orbital cellulitis as MISSING IDENTITY, no catalog identity existing for it despite being named in the located orbital cellulitis review.
